title: The Music That Continued
premise_public: Midway through a theater concert, the stage went dark and the pianist lifted both hands from the keyboard. The piano kept playing. Later, the stage crew confirmed that its loudspeakers had been disconnected.
solution_summary: The instrument was a self-playing acoustic piano fitted with mechanisms that pressed its real keys according to a programmed performance. The pianist had been miming along, and the piano's battery-backed control system kept moving the keys during the lighting failure. No loudspeaker playback was needed.

facts.text: The piano was a self-playing acoustic instrument with a mechanism that could press its keys.
A programmed performance controlled that mechanism rather than the performer's hands.
The key-playing mechanism had power independent of the stage lighting.
The notes came from the piano itself, not from the disconnected loudspeakers.
The performer was miming to the automatic performance.

acceptable_solutions: It was a self-playing acoustic piano whose motorized keys followed a program, even after the lights failed.
The pianist was miming while an automatic piano mechanism played the real keys using separate power.
A programmed player piano kept making acoustic music on backup power during the blackout.
hints: A piano can make sound without its keys being pressed by a person.
Consider what actually moved, and what supplied its power when the lights failed.
